## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dhammadāyāda Sutta* (MN 3, PTS MN i 12) is the third discourse in the *Mūlapariyāyavagga* of the *Majjhimanikāya* [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. In this discourse, the Buddha exhorts the monks to become heirs in the Dhamma (the spiritual path of contentment) rather than heirs in material possessions [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. Venerable Sāriputta subsequently elaborates on this exhortation, explaining how disciples should emulate the Buddha's conduct and train themselves in order to experience the fruits of the path [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995].
Curated parallels to the sutta exist in the Chinese Āgamas, specifically in the *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 88) and the *Ekottarika-āgama* (EĀ 18.3), although early comparative studies initially marked it as unidentified [SuttaCentral; Anesaki 1908]. Automatic alignments by DharmaNexus corroborate these relationships, identifying strong cross-language reuse matches with both the *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26) and *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125), as well as shared formulas in the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and Tibetan canonical works [DharmaNexus]. The sutta is also cited in post-canonical literature, notably in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 6.1.2) [SuttaCentral]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse between this discourse and other canonical suttas—including the *Araṇavibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 139), *Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta* (MN 9), and collections in the *Aṅguttaranikāya* and *Saṁyuttanikāya*—in addition to substantial quotation in the *Majjhimanikāya* commentary and sub-commentary [DharmaNexus].
